bull_bear.body: Final dividend INR 0.80/share (Total FY26 dividend INR 1.40/share, 70% payout); Disciplined capex for organic growth; Strategic JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso) for technology access without heavy upfront CAPEX; Focus on ROCE improvement via asset optimization.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity price volatility (geopolitical tensions); Labor cost inflation across states; Execution risk on new JV ramp-ups; Dependency on 2W/CV cycles though PV exposure increasing; Global economic slowdown impacting exports.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly confident and aggressive on growth; Emphasis on 'record-breaking' performance; Strategic focus on technology leadership (EV, electronics) and localization; Transparent on commodity challenges but assured of pass-through mechanisms.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Turntide JV brings unique axial flux motor technology (space-constrained applications) distinct from Flash Electronics' radial flux offerings, creating a complementary portfolio rather than cannibalization. Minda VAST consolidation is a step-change event for PV revenue mix, shifting the company's center of gravity towards higher-value 4W systems.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Shareholding page headed "Public & Other Shareholding" and "Strong Promoter Shareholding" shows 35.2% and 64.8%; the extracted text does not unambiguously map which percentage belongs to which label.
- Group structure lists Subsidiaries (Minda Instruments Ltd., Spark Minda Toyodenso, Spark Minda Green Mobility, Minda Vietnam, PT Minda Indonesia, Spark Minda Turntide) and JVs and Associates (Flash Electronics, Minda HCMF, Minda Vast, Minda Infac Pvt Ltd., EVQ Point, Minda Furukawa).
- Stake percentages printed on the schematic are 49.0%, 49.0%, 50.0%, 50.0%, 51.0%, 29.5% and 17.5%; seven values against six named JV/associate entities, so the name-to-stake mapping is not reliable from the extracted text.
- The deck states no dividend, buyback, debt, net-debt/equity or return-ratio policy.

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Commodity inflation and labor cost hikes pressuring margins across the auto ancillary sector. | Minda Corporation Ltd | beneficiary | High | Demonstrated ability to pass through 30-40% commodity costs while expanding EBITDA margins; operational excellence offsets wage hikes. |
| Need for advanced EV powertrain tech to secure premium OEM orders. | Minda Corporation Ltd | beneficiary | High | Turntide JV provides differentiated axial flux technology; Flash Electronics strengthens EV motor/controller portfolio; dual-engine strategy for EV. |
| Slow adoption of safety regulations like TPMS in India. | Minda Corporation Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Already secured orders and nearing SOP for TPMS across segments; regulatory tailwinds expected to drive volume. |
| Margin pressure on traditional component suppliers due to lack of pricing power. | Unorganized Tier-2/3 Suppliers | loser | Med | Minda's scale and pass-through contracts allow it to thrive, while smaller players without hedging or pricing clauses may suffer margin compression. |

deepdive.thesis: Minda Corp delivered record Q4/FY26 results with 29% Q4 revenue growth and margin expansion despite commodity inflation, driven by premiumization and strong volume growth across 2W/CV segments. The strategic consolidation of Minda VAST and new JVs (Turntide, Toyodenso) position the company to accelerate PV exposure and capture high-value EV powertrain opportunities, supporting a guided 20%+ CAGR towards INR 17,500 Cr by FY30.

open.item: Company spends about 5-6% of topline into depreciation/capex, of which 2-3% R&D, 1-2% greenfield, 1-2% maintenance.
Others segment expected to continue in the range of 15% to 17% of revenue for FY26.
Minda VAST (~INR 500 cr revenue, ~7% EBITDA, >90% PV) to be consolidated into Minda Corporation from FY27, accelerating PV mix to 25%.
Minda Instruments second plant ready by Q1 next year; die casting Noida operational, Pune fifth (export) plant ~18 months out.
Sunroof (INR 350 cr lifetime order) entering mass production in next 4-5 months; FY28 first full year revenue.
Toyodenso switches plant in mass production by March 2026; part starts Q2FY27, FY28 ramp year, first peak year ~FY29.
FY27 capex expected in the range of ~INR 400-450 cr (about 10% above the INR 350-400 cr run-rate).
Deploy the next tranche of the five-year capital expenditure plan in FY2026-27, funding capacity expansion at existing plants, greenfield facilities and future plant-expansion clusters.
Confirmed company should grow at least ~20% in FY27 to stay on track for Vision 2030.
Two-wheeler smart key share (~15%) expected to reach 20-25% by FY26-27; keyless penetration ~35-40% by 2030.
Reduce net Debt-to-Equity to 0.3x by FY2030, with organic free cash flow funding both the capex plan and the gradual reduction of net debt.
Triple exports to ₹15,000 Million under the Vision 2030 target, building a structural second growth engine beyond domestic volumes.
Reduce carbon intensity by 42% by 2030, aligned with the Science Based Targets initiative.
Long-term Vision 2030 to deliver INR 17,500 cr group consolidated top line (incl. Flash, VAST) with 12.5% EBITDA margin; requires ~19-20% growth.
Long-term vision to grow export business from ~INR 500 cr currently to INR 1,500 cr by 2030.
Apple-to-apple ROCE ~22% currently; committed to improve to 25% by 2030 via disciplined capital allocation.
Target to reduce ESG (emissions) by 42% by 2030.
Expects Indian sunroof market to reach about USD 500-600 million by 2030, with ~30% of vehicles having sunroof.
Target to reach at least 10% to 15% sunroof market share by FY2030 or FY2031.
Bring new product categories such as sunroofs and power tailgates to Start-of-Production, extending kit value per vehicle.
